market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the July 2026 meeting?
market.rules_text:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's July 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for July 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their July meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

data_availability.evidence_clause: The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.
data_availability.rationale: FOMC statements are publicly released immediately after the meeting and are permanently archived on the Federal Reserve's website. Data availability is essentially zero risk.

definitional_gaps.evidence_clause: If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket.
definitional_gaps.rationale: The rounding rule ('rounded up to the nearest 25') is somewhat unusual — rounding up always rather than to the nearest could create edge cases if an unconventional move occurs, but the 'No change' bracket is straightforward and the upper-bound definition is clear.

all_runs.load_bearing_clause: "If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the \"No change\" bracket."

resolver_discretion.rationale: Resolution is a mechanical check against the FOMC statement's stated upper bound. The rounding rule adds a small layer of interpretation but is clearly defined, leaving very little room for discretion.

This creates a real risk that the statement is issued after the market's technical end date, triggering the fallback 'No change' resolution regardless of the actual decision.
